text:
maria: heads up — noticed a p95 latency spike on continuous-batcher in us-west-2 at 13:02 UTC, small-token workloads (avg 8 tokens) went from ~220ms to ~310ms.
jon: I saw alerts, looks correlated with a kernel swap to the wave-optimized path. Any KV-cache signals around the same time?
carmen: yes, KV miss rate jumped from ~8% to ~33% for that pool. traces show more microbatches forming (smaller sizes) and the scheduler picking the wave kernel which is worse for tiny batches.
jon: ah that makes sense — wave kernels amortize well on large seqs but hurt tiny microbatches. kv churn -> shorter batch lifetimes -> weird kernel choice.
dave: quick idea: introduce a "gentle-overload" admission rule that prefers smaller non-wave batches when kv_miss > 20% and token_budget < 1k. also return a soft-defer (soft-429) with small retry_after to upstreams rather than hard queueing.
maria: agree. keep it conservative — we don't want throughput collapse. soft-defer should be a short polite backpressure so higher-level callers can retry or switch to cached/approx modes.
jon: can you propose a minimal config patch? small JSON patch would help ops roll this out behind a flag.
dave: here's a draft config snippet we tested locally:
```
{
  "admission_policy": "gentle-overload-v1",
  "token_budget_target": 1024,
  "max_microbatch_tokens": 2048,
  "kv_miss_threshold": 0.20,
  "soft_reject": {
    "enabled": true,
    "retry_after_ms": 50,
    "max_consecutive_soft_rejects": 3
  },
  "kernel_hint": "prefetch_friendly"
}
```
carmen: nice. add an adaptive scale: if kv_miss > 30% then reduce token_budget_target by 10% (to favor smaller batches) and flip kernel_hint to "non-wave".
jon: we should also surface kernel_switch_count and kv_miss_rate to the console dashboard (per-pool, per-model) — helps debug rollouts.
perf-bot: perf-run summary (canary stub): baseline: p95=280ms p50=85ms throughput=100rps. patch(gentle-overload): p95=220ms p50=90ms throughput=98rps. tail reduced ~21% at cost of ~2% throughput.
maria: that's promising — tail improvement definitely helps SLOs. we need cost math: 2% throughput down could be acceptable if p95 SLA gains avoid client retries.
dave: plan: implement behind feature flag, add metric emission: kv_miss_rate, microbatch_size_hist, kernel_choice_rate, soft_reject_rate. Canary target: 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 4 hours.
carmen: tests: add a perf test that injects synthetic KV misses to validate adaptive token_budget and kernel hint switch. also add unit tests for soft_reject backoff counters.
jon: who picks this up? I can do the admission-policy PR + unit tests. dave can wire metrics and feature flag. maria can own the canary rollout and dashboard tiles.
maria: sounds good. I'll schedule the canary Tue morning and pre-warm observability.
dave: one more: add a short doc blurb for API clients about the soft-reject response shape (we'll return HTTP 429 with header `X-Soft-Backoff: 50` and a json body: { "retry_after_ms": 50, "reason": "kv-prefetch" }).
jon: ack. I'll include that in the PR description.
maria: 👍 thanks. turning this into issues: #eng-runtime-ticket-487 (admission policy PR), #eng-runtime-ticket-488 (metrics + flag), #eng-runtime-ticket-489 (canary + runbook).
dave: leaving notes for oncall: if soft_reject_rate > 10% for >10m, rollback flag. Also alert if kernel_switch_count spikes > 3x baseline.
carmen: bah — long thread but good plan. small followup: ensure the kernel-selector has a clear precedence: explicit kernel_hint > auto-latency-based selection.
maria: agreed. we'll add that precedence rule to the selector doc.
jon: ok merging action items. ping me if you want a quick pairing session on the PR.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
